actions.action: Check the leaf base to confirm the ID
Water slowly until it drains, then let the top 1-2 inches dry before watering again
Check the roots for root-binding before repotting
After a few weeks, repot 1-2 inches larger into a heavy pot with well-draining mix plus perlite or bark
If not root-bound, refresh the top layer of soil instead
Gradually move to brighter light, starting with indirect light or a sheer curtain
Use the grow light as a winter supplement
Move the plant away from cold glass and drafts at the sliding door
Feed with balanced fertilizer at half strength in spring and summer
Inspect leaf undersides and the crown for mealybugs and scale
Test a mild dish soap spray on one leaf, spray, then rinse off
Alternatively, use insecticidal soap or neem
Post a close-up of a leaf base and any flowers

reason: The answer misidentifies the Crinum as Curculigo and calls the plant mostly fine, but it does tie the drooping to low light and covers bright light, warmth and a perlite mix among many other steps; nothing it suggests is likely to hurt the plant.
